title: Failover conductor: readiness heuristics and canary simulator
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: Implement a centralized "failover conductor" that evaluates inter-region readiness using a heuristic health matrix and a lightweight canary simulator. This work aims to reduce noisy failovers, improve deterministic cutovers, and make warm-standby activation predictable across Dedicated and Private deployments. The conductor will be policy-driven (region preferences, tier routing rules, model variant fallbacks) and expose a canary simulation API to validate readiness before routing changes are applied.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Conductor exposes a readiness score per region (0-100) derived from latency, KV-cache warmth, model-variant availability, and capacity margins.
2) Canary simulator can run N synthetic sessions that exercise prefix cache, KV replay, and model-variant downgrade paths without impacting production traffic.
3) Automated gating prevents a region switch if readiness < configured threshold or if simulated SLA regressions are observed.
4) End-to-end test (in staging) demonstrates a graceful cutover sequence with rollback under degraded conditions.
5) Telemetry dashboards and alerts created: readiness-score, canary-failure-rate, fallback-activation-counts.
design_notes:
Heuristic health matrix fields:
- latency_p95: weighted by route SLA importance
- kv_cache_heat: percentage of commonly used prefixes present
- active_shards: fraction of target serving shards up and synced
- variant_compatibility: whether fallback model variant supports required ops
- throttling_headroom: available QPS margin for soft ramp
Score computation is a weighted sum with configurable policy weights per customer tier. The conductor will use a two-phase activation: preflight (simulation + passive probes) and live switchover (traffic ramp + continuous verification).
Policy examples: prefer-region-by-geo then by-cost; tier-routing can prefer dedicated pools for P0 customers. Fallbacks: when exact model variant isn't available, system selects nearest compatible quantized variant and marks it as degraded mode in the scoreboard.
implementation_plan:
1) Define schema for readiness telemetry and implement collectors in the serving runtime (ENG + infra) (2w).
2) Build canary-simulator service that replays synthetic sessions and measures critical signals (2w).
3) Conductor control plane: policy engine, score calculator, and action sequencer (3w).
4) Integrate with routing layer to perform phased traffic ramp and automatic rollback (2w).
5) Create staging pipelines and runbook (1w).
Key deliverables: readiness API, canary-simulator CLI/API, conductor UI hooks in Console, Grafana dashboards, runbook.
MVP scope excludes multi-tenant quota-aware throttles (follow-up).
testing_plan:
- Unit tests for score calculator and policy evaluation.
- Integration tests: simulate region degradation and assert conductor blocks/reroutes as policy dictates.
- Staging canary: run 100 synthetic sessions with 5 variant-downgrades and verify no SLA violation in primary region and acceptable degraded metrics in fallback.
- Chaos experiment: time-boxed region outage in staging to validate switch and rollback sequences.
- Performance: canary simulator should not exceed 5% of target region QPS when run in passive mode.
telemetry_and_alerting:
Required metrics: readiness_score, readiness_components_{latency,kv,shards,variant,headroom}, canary_simulation_pass_rate, fallback_activation_count, rollback_count, time_to_recover.
Dashboards: per-region readiness heatmap, recent canary simulation history, active rollout traces.
Alerts: readiness_score < threshold for >2m, canary_fail_rate >5% for two consecutive runs, rollback_count spike >3/hour.
risks_and_mitigations:
Risk: False positives from noisy KV cache signals causing unnecessary blocks. Mitigation: apply smoothing window and require corroborating signals (latency and active_shards) before gating.
Risk: Canary simulator accidentally perturbs production path. Mitigation: run in isolated passive mode by default and require opt-in to active replay; add strict rate limits and tagging.
Risk: Policy complexity yields unexpected routing decisions. Mitigation: ship with conservative default policy and enable advanced policies behind feature flag; provide dry-run mode in Console.
